8

Three Ways To Manage Context

Context strategies keep one agent and manage what it sees. Agentic patterns split the work across agents.

Context strategy

Compress it

Keep one agent; shrink its history to fit the window.

Context strategy

Fetch it

Keep one agent; pull in only what the step needs.

Agentic patterns

Split it

Spread work across agents, each with its own slice.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

9

Five Multi-Agent Orchestration Patterns

Same agents, five different ways to coordinate them.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

10

Sequential Orchestration

Agents are chained in a predefined order. Each one processes the previous agent’s output.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

11

Bug Triage to Pull Request

Trigger: an e-commerce store's checkout fails with HTTP 500 errors after release 2.14.1, and Sentry raises an alert.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

12

Concurrent Orchestration

Agents work on the same input at the same time. A collector combines their results.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

13

Parallel Pull Request Review

Trigger: a pull request is opened and needs a review from several angles.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

14

Group Chat Orchestration

Agents discuss in one shared thread. A chat manager decides who speaks and when to stop.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

15

Database Migration Review

Trigger: a schema migration needs agreement before it goes to production.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

16

Handoff Orchestration

Agents pass full control to one another until the right one resolves the task.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

17

Deployment Failure Support

Trigger: a developer reports that orders-service pods are stuck in ImagePullBackOff.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

18

Magentic Orchestration

A manager builds and revises a task ledger with specialist agents, then executes the plan.

AI AGENT ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS

19

Latency Regression Investigation

Trigger: p99 latency doubled after release 2.14.2 and nobody knows why.

The model brings the capability. The agentic pattern helps you manage speed, cost and data organization.

Choosing a Pattern

Two questions: does everything fit in the context window, and does each step depend on the last?

Data
scale

Task dependence

Split the work

Speed
Concurrent

Parallel workers, each with a clean window

Subagents

A lead agent delegates; each subagent returns a short summary

Keep the state compact

Cost
Summary or notes

Compress the history; one agent keeps going

Knowledge graph

Fetch only the facts each step needs

Magentic

A manager keeps a compact task ledger

Sequential

Fixed stages, each passing on a compact result

One agent, or parallel for speed

CostSpeed
Single agent

The default: same accuracy, lowest cost

Concurrent

Only to cut wait time, or to vote over runs

One agent

Cost
Single agent

Splitting adds handoff loss, not accuracy

Handoff

When steps need different tools or permissions

Group Chat

When you want a debate; expect no gain over voting

Agentic patternContext strategyData governance

Any pattern that splits the work can also scope each agent’s data and access.

Appendix: When to Use Each Pattern

Sequential

Use when

Fixed stages, each building on the last.

Context

Each agent sees only the previous output.

Watch out for

Details lost between stages; the slowest option.

Our evidence

Partly tested

Workers in series match parallel accuracy but take about twice as long.

Concurrent

Use when

Independent subtasks, or several takes on one input, when speed matters.

Context

Each worker starts with a clean window.

Watch out for

2–3× the tokens; results to merge.

Our evidence

Tested

About 20 points over one agent on 32 suppliers. Voting matches debate at equal cost.

Group Chat

Use when

You want a debate or review between perspectives.

Context

One shared thread that grows every turn.

Watch out for

About 5× the cost; slow to converge.

Our evidence

Tested

A debating council is expected to do no better than voting at the same cost.

Handoff

Use when

Steps need different skills, tools or permissions.

Context

The next agent gets only what is handed over.

Watch out for

Handoffs drop context; routing loops.

Our evidence

Partly tested

Specialist roles expected to add nothing beyond isolation. Permissions are judgement.

Magentic

Use when

Open-ended work where the plan emerges, or approvals need a record.

Context

A manager’s task ledger holds the plan; specialists get focused tasks.

Watch out for

Loops and unpredictable cost; the manager’s context grows.

Our evidence

Not tested

From practice.

Expected

Specialise for permissions, ownership and maintainability, not for accuracy.
